marks.gloss_en: תא שמע: 'המית שורי את פלוני... הרי זה משלם על פי עצמו' -- מאי לאו בתם? if even a tam pays on his own admission, the payment is mamona!

לא, במועד -- and against the challenge 'then let the mishnah split its own case rather than move to the slave clause' (15b.3-4), the answer's standing form: כולה במועד קמיירי, the entire mishnah speaks of a muad.

אין... תיובתא והלכתא?! (15b.10) -- yes: the teyuvta rested only on the tanna's not teaching 'as much as he damaged' (15b.11), and לא פסיקא ליה -- because chatzi nezek of tzerorot is mamona by received tradition, no clean rule could be stated (15b.12). The refutation's basis dissolves; knasa is held again.
והלכתא: פלגא נזקא קנסא -- the redactor rules for the side the teyuvta of 15b.8 refuted; coherent only because 15b.11-12 blunts the refutation. Recorded as L0 data; the engine derives nothing from it.
the mishnah (Ketubot 41a): one who admits 'my ox killed so-and-so' or 'so-and-so's ox' pays based on his own admission
the closing clause of that mishnah: זה הכלל -- anyone who pays more than the damage he caused does not pay based on his own admission
והשתא דאמרת פלגא נזקא קנסא: an innocuous dog that ate lambs or a cat that ate a chicken is meshune -- keren-type -- and the fine is not collected by the courts in Bavel
this applies to large prey; small prey is the animal's normal way (shen), full damages, collected in Bavel
if the injured party seized the damager's property for the fine, we do not take it back from him
if he asks for a court date in Eretz Yisrael we fix one, and excommunicate the damager if he does not go
either way we excommunicate him until he removes the danger -- מדרבי נתן (the basis is R. Natan's baraita, 15b.18)
R. Natan's baraita: one may not raise a vicious dog or keep an unstable ladder in his house -- לא תשים דמים בביתך

since it teaches 'the tooth is muad to eat', the clause must speak of the injured party's courtyard (shen is exempt in the public domain) -- and 'the animal is not muad' there means it pays half for the unusual
the Rabbanan: keren-type damage in the injured party's courtyard is unusual (משונה) and pays half damages
R. Tarfon: unusual keren-type damage in the injured party's courtyard pays full damages
Shmuel to Rav Yehuda: sharp one, leave the mishnah and follow me -- the first clause is the Rabbanan and the later clause is R. Tarfon
